cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to God's chosen people living as exiles, scattered across Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia. He's just told them they have a living hope and an inheritance kept in heaven for them that can't perish, can't be spoiled and won't fade. Now Peter's done telling them what they HAVE, and he's about to tell them how to LIVE.
First thing Peter says: prepare your minds for action and be sober-minded. That's not the snooze button, friend, that's both feet on the floor with the apron already ON.

cards.question: Peter wants their minds ready and clear. Where does he tell them to set their hope fully?

answers.text: On the grace coming when Jesus Christ is revealed
On the day their years as exiles finally end
On the reward their faithful work will earn them

cards.text: Then Peter calls them obedient children and brings up the passions of their former ignorance. You know, the old days. The stuff we look back on and go, "Why did I think that was a GOOD idea?"

cards.question: Peter tells these obedient children to keep shaping their lives around the passions of their former ignorance.

cards.text: So instead, Peter sets the bar: be holy in all you do. Not some of the batches, friend. Not MOST of the batches. ALL of them, even the lopsided last one off the tray.

cards.question: Peter backs up his call to be holy with Scripture. Why should they be holy?

answers.text: Because the One who called them is holy
Because their neighbors are watching them closely
Because being holy keeps their troubles away

cards.text: Then Peter reminds them who they call on: a Father who judges each one's work. And friend, I've made some batches I'd REALLY rather He skipped.

cards.question: The Father Peter talks about judges each one's work without playing favorites.
Since their Father judges each one's work, Peter tells them to live in reverent ___ during their stay as foreigners.

cards.text: Peter reminds them they were redeemed from the empty way of life handed down from their forefathers. Like inheriting the family recipe box, opening it up, and finding... just the box.

cards.question: Peter says the price of their redemption was paid in silver or gold.
Not silver and not gold. So what does Peter say they were redeemed with?

cards.text: Peter calls Christ a lamb without blemish or spot. Friend, that's the Lamb whose Supper we're filling these cookie boxes for (Revelation 19:9).
And this was no last-minute plan: He was known before the foundation of the world. Not like me, deciding what to bake while the oven's already beeping at me.

cards.question: Christ was known before the foundation of the world. When was He revealed, and for whose sake?

answers.text: In the last times for their sake
In the days of Moses for Israel's sake
At the very beginning for the angels' sake

cards.question: Through Christ they believe in God, who ___ Him from the dead and ___ Him. So their faith and hope are in God.

cards.text: Next, Peter turns to how they treat each other: they've purified their souls by obeying the truth, so now they have a genuine love for their brothers. GENUINE, friend, not the "we should totally get together sometime" kind.

cards.question: Their love for their brothers is already genuine. So what does Peter tell them to do with it?

answers.text: Love one another deeply from a pure heart
Keep their love within their own households
Share their love with those who love them back

cards.text: Peter says they've been born again, not of perishable seed but of imperishable. Friend, I know a little something about being made new, and let me tell you, it beats the back of a drawer EVERY time.

cards.question: Peter says this new birth came through something. What is it?

answers.text: The living and enduring word of God
The faithful work of the apostles
The long line of their forefathers

cards.text: Then Peter quotes Scripture: all flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field (Isaiah 40:6). That's everybody, friend, me included, and I'm counting this mustache as GLORY.

cards.question: In the Scripture Peter quotes, the grass and the flowers of the field last forever.
The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the ___ of the Lord stands forever.

cards.text: Peter wraps it up: "And this is the word that was proclaimed to you." The word that stands forever, friend, and somebody brought it right to THEM.
